It's an exaggerated pejorative term. The "warrior" is meant to point out the over zealous nature of the people the term is meant to describe. It has nothing to do with actual justice, but rather people screaming loudly over things they perceive to be unjust (and other people screaming back at them).

Yes, it was intended to be a sarcastic pejorative by people who felt that SJWs were far more interested in methods that drew attention to themselves than ones which were effective in advancing anything recognisable as positive social justice outcomes.

They used it to refer to themselves. Then places like /r/tumblrinaction appeared. Since their primary goal was to find them so that they could make fun of them, it made since to call them what they called themselves, since that's what it would be tagged under. From there, those users started to leak into other places, using the same (albeit ironic) vocabulary.

Nah, I think I would dispute that. As someone who started on tumblr before migrating to reddit (and now to voat), I'd venture that it started as a pejorative, and then was increasingly adopted by the people it was used on-- first ironically and then wholly unironically.

This paper from 2001 is the earliest reliably-dated source I could find for the term. This isn't to say that it wasn't used before then, just that I can't find it. The fact that the paper calls the definition "new" seems to imply that it arose somewhere around that time. It was clearly used non-ironically to start with. My guess is that a number of the most over the top SJW types used the term to refer to themselves, and it was seen as so laughable that their opponents started using it as an insult against them. "Social justice" was a big real-world meme in the 90's (at least where I was at the time), so it seems likely it was born out of that. Exactly when the meaning was corrupted, I don't know.
